To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The most important factor influencing the health and safety administration in New Zealand firms was government regulation.

The factors influencing health and safety performance are: (1) the quality of the relationship between the union and the firm; (2) the degree of government regulation; (3) the level of employee concern and the degree to which employees are involved in safety administration; and (4) the locus of ownership.

(1) The quality of the health and safety administration is significantly influenced by the nature of the relationship with unions; (2) The quality of health and safety is influenced by the degree to which the organization is unionized and whether it is a state-owned enterprise; (3) The quality of accident performance is influenced by the nature and quality of the relationship between the organization and its unions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between health and safety administration and accident performance.
the relationship between the organizational and environmental context of health and safety management and subsequent safety performance.
the relationship between the internal and external environment and its effect on the health and safety administration of firms in New Zealand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the factors influencing safety performance are complex and varied.
health and safety performance in the industrial sector is a function of a number of interacting factors.
the more complex the organizational structure, the greater the need to have a well-organized safety programme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a number of external pressures, such as government regulations, are the major factors in determining the level of health and safety performance in an organization.

the factors which influence the effectiveness of safety administration are not only the internal ones of management commitment and employee involvement, but also the external factors of union involvement and government regulation.
there is no single factor or group of factors that is more important in determining health and safety performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the factors that shape the administration of health safety policies are not necessarily related to the accident performance of the organization.
there are a number of environmental pressures which influence the effectiveness of health safety administration.
the health and safety performance of an organization is influenced by the interaction of multiple factors.
